about.title: Yuba City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Sutter County's public crash records show 254 injury collisions in Yuba City last year, with 348 people hurt and 2 lives lost — numbers that reflect real neighbors dealing with real recovery. Corridors like Rt 20, Rt 99, Bridge Street, and Garden Highway see a steady mix of local and through traffic, and Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. show up often in reported crashes. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memories can fade or disappear. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and the attorneys in our network only get paid if you recover compensation.
commonInjuries: Cuts, bruising, and lacerations from impact

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a city road crew or public bus) was involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible, you may still recover a share of damages — but insurers often try to shift blame onto you early on. Having someone review the facts before you speak with an adjuster can protect your position.

items.title: Recorded Statements Aren't Required Right Away
items.desc: The other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement soon after the crash — you're not obligated to give one, and it can be used to minimize your claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Yuba City car accident?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes six months. It's worth getting a quick review of your situation so you don't miss a filing window.

items.question: Does it matter that Rt 20 and Bridge Street see a lot of reported crashes?
items.answer: Public crash data shows these corridors, along with Rt 99 and Garden Highway, account for a notable share of Yuba City's injury collisions, particularly on Friday evenings. That pattern doesn't determine fault in any individual case, but an attorney reviewing your crash location and timing can factor in available reports and camera footage from nearby businesses.

items.question: Will I owe anything if I talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and the independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to hire anyone after speaking with them.
